items.t: How Many Shares of Duke Energy, Southern Company or WEC Energy Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
sum: - A hypothetical retiree would need about $364,600 of Duke Energy, $374,800 of Southern Company or $374,900 of WEC Energy Group to collect $1,000 a month in dividends at today’s prices.
- All three cover their dividends comfortably, paying out 67% to 68% of normalized earnings in fiscal 2025, with Southern Company the least covered.
- WEC Energy Group costs the most up front, but its dividend grew 7.1% a year from fiscal 2020 to fiscal 2025, and it plans raises of 6.5% to 7% from here.
- WEC’s faster-growing check looks worth the about $10,300 extra it costs over Duke Energy.

Any retiree hunting for a dividend check they can count on is going to look at utilities like Duke Energy (DUK), Southern Company (SO) and WEC Energy Group (WEC). And all three just reported third quarters lifted by data center demand.
Let’s take a hypothetical retiree who wants $1,000 a month, or $12,000 a year, from just one of them.

At today’s prices, Duke takes 2,765 shares, or about $364,600. Southern takes 3,948 shares, about $374,800, and WEC takes 3,150 shares, about $374,900. That’s about $10,300 between the cheapest check and the priciest, so it’s worth knowing what the extra money gets you.

Southern Company stock: Leadership changes set for January
sum: Southern Company announced a broad leadership reshuffle on November 19, with the changes set to take effect on January 1, 2027. The company said the appointments are intended to align operations with rising energy demand, infrastructure investment and technological change, according to the CSRwire release.

Kim Greene, currently chairman, president and CEO of Georgia Power, will become president of Southern Company Operations. Her responsibilities will include system operations, generation, transmission, planning, nuclear assets, enterprise strategy and technology-related priorities.

Stan Connally, Southern Company's executive vice president and chief operating officer, will become chairman, president and CEO of Georgia Power. The subsidiary serves more than 2.8 million customers across 155 Georgia counties, and Connally will focus on reliability, infrastructure and predictable rates.

The company also plans to expand Chief Legal Officer Sterling Spainhour's remit to include the Technology Organization. Chief Human Resources Officer Sloane Drake will take responsibility for systemwide training, linking workforce development more closely to changing technology needs.

For investors, the appointments put execution capacity at the center of Southern Company's growth plans. Bringing nuclear generation together with the wider generation portfolio could support more integrated planning and investment, while the Georgia Power change places a senior operating executive at the head of the group's largest subsidiary.

sum: - At today’s prices, $1,000 a month in dividends takes about $368,800 of WEC Energy Group, about $367,700 of Southern Company or about $402,200 of NextEra Energy.
- WEC Energy’s check costs the least, and the company plans dividend growth of 6.5% to 7% a year, faster than Southern’s recent pace and the 6% NextEra plans after 2026.

- Virginia’s hearings on NextEra’s merger with Dominion Energy, which began Nov. 16, are the next big thing to watch for the priciest check.
If you’re counting on dividends to cover some of your bills in retirement, utilities like Southern Company (SO), NextEra Energy (NEE) and WEC Energy Group (WEC) are probably on your list.

Southern Company’s $100 Billion Spending Plan Puts Its Dividend Growth to the Test
sum: Southern Company (NYSE:SO | SO Price Prediction) has raised its dividend for 25 consecutive years[1], and its latest quarter was strong. Investors now want to know whether a capital plan that “could potentially approach $100 billion”[1] still leaves room for a 26th raise.

On April 20, 2026, the board raised the quarterly payout from $0.74 to $0.76 per share, a 2.7% increase. The forward annual rate of $3.04 works out to a 3.26% yield at the $93.34 share price. On the November 5 call, CEO Chris Womack summed up the company’s case:

“When you combine these and other factors with 25 consecutive years of dividend increases, more than three-quarters of a century having never reduced our dividend, 8% EPS growth with upside, and our strong credit metrics, our value proposition objective of superior risk-adjusted total shareholder return is second to none.”[1]

Third-quarter adjusted EPS came in at $1.94, ahead of the $1.71 consensus. Revenue rose 13.0% to $8.843 billion. CFO David Poroch expects full-year adjusted earnings of $4.70[1], which is $0.10 above the top of the original guidance range. On that figure, the forward dividend uses about 65% of earnings. Poroch also said management feels able to raise the upper end of its 2027 and 2028 guidance.

Here is how a regulated utility pays its dividend. State commissions set the rates customers pay and the return the company can earn on its rate base, which is the plants and power lines it has built. A bigger rate base means more allowed earnings. The catch is that the company has to borrow money and sell stock to build those assets before it can earn on them. Southern has also committed to “holding base rates flat in Alabama and Georgia until at least 2029,”[1] so for now its growth has to come from selling more power.

Data center usage rose 59%[1] in the quarter. Signed large-load contracts reached 21 gigawatts[1], and another 7 gigawatts are in late stages. Poroch said these customers’ minimum bills cover “at least 100% of the cost being introduced into the system.”[1] Womack added:
“We are seeing the highest level of weather-normal sales growth in generations.”[1]

How Is Data-Center Demand Lifting Southern Company (NYSE:SO) Growth?
sum: - Southern Company pointed to a sharp rise in Southeast electricity demand led by data centers and new industry across its territory
- Its newly completed nuclear units at Plant Vogtle are supplying firm, round-the-clock power into that growing load
- The update arrived during a choppy, rotation-heavy week that kept utilities and clean-power names under a bright spotlight

Southern Company (NYSE:SO) Utilities Southern Company (NYSE:SO) 93.29 USD +0.010 0.011% Last Updated at: 2026-11-19T21:01:00Z came into sharper view this week as attention turned to the sheer scale of electricity demand building across its Southeastern service territory. Its shares are tracked within the S&P 500, NYSE Composite and Russell 1000. The company has described a step-change in load, driven above all by data centers chasing power for artificial-intelligence computing, alongside new factories and a broader wave of economic activity across Georgia and neighboring states. For a large regulated utility, that kind of demand growth is the clearest sign of a shifting business environment in years. For readers who follow Utility Stocks, Southern Company remains a closely watched name in the group.

The demand story across Southern Company's footprint has shifted dramatically in a short span. For years, electricity usage in its territory grew slowly, in line with population and modest commercial activity. That baseline has been upended by a rush of large-load customers, with data centers at the forefront, drawn to the region by available land, a business-friendly climate and the promise of power. The company now describes a pipeline of prospective load that dwarfs anything it planned for in the recent past.

At the center of Southern Company's supply story sits Plant Vogtle, where the recently completed reactors stand as the newest large nuclear units built in the country in a generation. Bringing them online was a long and closely watched undertaking, and their arrival gives the company a substantial block of firm, carbon-free electricity precisely when round-the-clock power has become the scarcest and most prized resource on the grid.
The broader utility group has been one of the market's most talked-about corners this year, and the reason traces back to demand.

The bigger picture confirms it. Southern's price sits well above its 50-day average of 89.03, and the 20-day average itself is above the 50-day — a stance that typically signals buyers in control over the medium term. There is no new moving-average crossover to report: the setup has been in place rather than forming on this session. What matters more for readers watching the chart is where the stock sits inside its recent range. Wednesday's close left the shares at 93% of the 20-day range, with support at 91.52 and resistance at 94.64 — a level the stock is now knocking against. The three-month high of 95.72 and low of 81.69 frame how far the recovery has run.

Momentum is the mixed part of the story. The relative strength index (RSI, a 0–100 measure of buying intensity) reads 59.8 — neutral, meaning the advance has not stretched into overbought territory where the rally would look exhausted. The stochastic oscillator, which compares the close to its recent range, is also neutral, at %K 75.4 against %D 71.7. Yet the MACD — a trend-following gauge built from moving averages — is the outlier. Its reading of 1.267 sits below the signal line at 1.398, leaving a negative histogram of −0.131. In plain terms: the longer trend is up, but short-term momentum has cooled. That is the sort of divergence that often accompanies a pause before a stock either re-accelerates or pulls back.

Volatility is the sleeper signal. The Bollinger band width — a measure of how spread out recent prices have been — has narrowed to 3.3%, a condition traders call a squeeze. A squeeze means the market is coiling, and historically such compression has preceded outsized moves in either direction, though it says nothing about which way. The stock's average true range (ATR, a measure of daily swing) is 1.97 USD, or about 2.1% of the price — moderate volatility. The upper Bollinger band rests at 94.90 and the lower at 91.80, with the price at 84% of the band width (%B), putting it close to the upper edge. Volume is the caution flag.

Southern Company stock completes $2 billion corporate-unit offering
sum: Southern Company completed its corporate-unit offering on November 17, according to a Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The utility sold 40 million Corporate Units after underwriters exercised their full option for additional units, completing a financing that was initially announced at a smaller size.

Each unit has a stated amount of 50 U.S. dollars. It combines a contract requiring the holder to purchase a specified number of Southern Company's common shares for 50 U.S. dollars no later than December 15, 2029, with beneficial interests in two series of remarketable senior notes.

The note interests relate to Series 2026C securities due in 2031 and Series 2026D securities due in 2034. Southern Company said total annual distributions on the units will equal 8.625% of the stated amount. That rate consists of quarterly contract-adjustment payments of 3.125% and interest of 5.50% on the senior notes.

The senior notes serve as collateral for the obligation to purchase common stock. They may be remarketed before the applicable settlement date under the terms of the purchase contract and pledge agreement. The filing identifies BofA Securities and Barclays Capital as representatives for the underwriters and U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee and agent for the related agreements.

For investors in the common stock, the structure combines an immediate capital-raising transaction with a future equity commitment. The purchase contracts can increase the number of common shares outstanding when they settle, making the eventual settlement terms relevant to per-share earnings and ownership considerations. The distribution rate may support demand for the units, but it does not remove the obligation to assess the effect of future share issuance.

Hunton Advises on The Southern Company’s Equity Units Offering
sum: Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP advised the underwriters on The Southern Company’s (the “Company”) SEC-registered offering of 40 million equity units (initially consisting of 40 million corporate units), which included an additional 5 million corporate units purchased pursuant to the full exercise of the overallotment option.

The Southern Company is the parent company of three traditional electric operating companies, Southern Power Company and Southern Company Gas. The traditional electric operating companies — Alabama Power Company, Georgia Power Company and Mississippi Power Company — are each operating public utility companies providing electric services to retail customers in three Southeastern states of the United States in addition to wholesale customers in the Southeast. Southern Power Company develops, constructs, acquires, owns, operates and manages power generation assets, including renewable energy projects, and sells electricity at market-based rates in the wholesale market. Southern Company Gas is an energy services holding company whose primary business is the distribution of natural gas in four states – Illinois, Georgia, Virginia and Tennessee – through the natural gas distribution utilities. Southern Company Gas is also involved in several other businesses that are complementary to the distribution of natural gas.

The Hunton team included Peter K. O’Brien, Steven C. Friend, Patrick C. Jamieson, Monika M. Dziewa, Jingyi “Alice” Yao and Nancy Xu. Robert McNamara, William Freeman and David Kamins provided tax advice. Leslie Okinaka provided ERISA advice.

sum: The Southern Company SO has gained momentum since the beginning of the year, with its share price gaining 8.6%. Additionally, its performance outpaced both the Zacks Utility-Electric Power industry’s growth of 3.8% and the broader utility sector’s rise of nearly 3.1%. This outperformance signals relative strength and highlights the company’s favorable positioning. With such momentum, investors have to be wondering, will the recent trend continue or is Southern Company due for a pullback?

Founded in 1945 and headquartered in Atlanta, GA, Southern Company is one of the largest U.S. utilities, serving about nine million electricity and natural gas customers. Its operations include regulated electric utilities, wholesale power generation and natural gas distribution. Through Southern Power, the company operates a diversified portfolio across gas, solar, wind and storage assets, supported by long-term power purchase agreements. Southern Company Gas serves 4.4 million customers through an extensive pipeline network and storage facilities across several U.S. states.

However, for investors, the key debate is whether SO’s strong run has more room to extend or if the rally has priced in much of the upside. With the company’s diversified portfolio strategy and recent tailwinds playing a critical role, the stock’s prospects warrant a closer examination before deciding whether to buy, hold or take profits.

Accelerating Data Center Demand Supports Long-Term Growth: Southern Company is positioned to benefit from accelerating electricity demand across the southeastern United States, particularly from data centers and other large commercial customers. Its contracted large-load portfolio has reached approximately 21 gigawatts (GW), with another 7 GW in advanced development stages. Importantly, data center electricity usage increased 59% in the third quarter of 2026, demonstrating that previously contracted demand is beginning to translate into actual consumption. Continued expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure and commercial operations should create opportunities for higher electricity sales, additional infrastructure investment and sustained earnings growth.

History Says This Dividend Stock Can Protect Your Portfolio if a Stock Market Slump Is Coming
sum: With the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.40%) hovering near all-time highs despite geopolitical conflicts, high inflation, and concerns around an AI bubble, investors are worried about a stock market slump. Southern Company (SO +1.21%) can help, but you have to look at the full picture to understand why. And that means considering both the stock price and the importance of collecting a reliable dividend. Here's what you need to know.

Wall Street tends to throw the baby out with the bathwater when a bear market hits. So there aren't many places to hide. Usually, the best you can hope for is to own stocks that don't go down as much as the market. Southern Company has outperformed, meaning it didn't fall as much, during three of the last four bear markets.

The oddball in that mix was the bear market associated with the coronavirus pandemic, when Southern's stock fell slightly more than the S&P 500 index. That downturn, however, was an unusual one because of the economic shutdowns used to slow the spread of the illness. That hit utilities hard because investors feared that business-related revenues would collapse. Luckily, Southern Company survived the period just fine. On the whole, if you are looking for a safe place in a storm, Southern Company looks like a good option.

That said, regulated utilities are known for both their reliable businesses and their reliable dividends. On the dividend front, Southern Company is a standout. For starters, it offers an attractive dividend yield of 3.2% as of this writing. The S&P's yield is a tiny 1% or so. That allows you to focus on collecting an above-market dividend rather than on stock prices during a downturn.

You can take further comfort from the fact that the dividend has been increased annually for 25 years. However, even that isn't the whole picture, because the dividend has been increased or held steady for 79 years. When investors are facing the next bear market, history suggests that Southern will not only see less of a hit to its share price, but that investors can comfortably focus on its dividend instead of its stock price.
Staying invested through a deep market downturn is emotionally difficult.

Southern Company stock faces $1.75 billion equity-unit offering
sum: Southern Company priced a new equity-unit offering on Thursday, November 12, as the utility seeks additional funding for debt management and corporate investment. The company disclosed the transaction in a Southern Company release.

The offering comprises 35 million Series A Equity Units with a stated amount of 50 US dollars each, for an aggregate stated amount of 1.75 billion US dollars. Each unit combines a contract to purchase Southern Company common stock in the future with fractional interests in two series of remarketable senior notes.

Annual distributions are set at 8.625 percent. The transaction is expected to close on Tuesday, November 17, subject to customary closing conditions. The company also granted the underwriters an option for up to 5 million additional units to cover over-allotments.

Southern Company expects net proceeds of about 1.724 billion US dollars before other offering expenses, or 1.970 billion US dollars if the over-allotment option is exercised in full. About 135.3 million US dollars is intended for the repurchase of approximately 125.8 million US dollars of convertible notes due in June 2027.

The remaining proceeds are earmarked for short-term debt repayment and general corporate purposes, including investments in subsidiaries. The company serves 9 million customers across the Southeast and beyond through its operating businesses.

The equity units create a new financing obligation and include a future stock-purchase requirement no later than December 15, 2029, subject to the terms disclosed in the offering. Investors will therefore weigh the additional funding against Southern Company's capital needs and its plans for continued energy infrastructure investment.

Southern Company stock: 2026 earnings outlook rises to $4.70
sum: Southern Company is lifting its earnings outlook as power demand from data centers accelerates. A November 12 report by Quotelinks said the utility raised its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings target to approximately 4.70 US dollars per share after third-quarter adjusted earnings reached 1.94 US dollars per share.

The report said data center electricity use rose 59 percent year over year in the third quarter and 52 percent during the first nine months of 2026. Weather-adjusted commercial electricity sales increased 7.3 percent, while weather-normalized retail sales grew 3.5 percent.

Southern Company had about 21 gigawatts of signed contracts with large-load customers at the end of the third quarter, according to the report. A further 7 gigawatts of potential business remained under advanced negotiation across Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia.

The demand outlook also carries substantial capital requirements. Chief Financial Officer David Poroch outlined roughly 4 billion US dollars of additional infrastructure investment beyond the existing 81 billion US dollar base capital program. The projects include natural gas facilities, pipeline expansion and nuclear upgrades linked to a partnership with Google. The five-year capital budget could approach 100 billion US dollars if further projects receive regulatory approval.

Southern Company expects remaining equity needs of about 2 billion US dollars through 2030 and is targeting a funds-from-operations-to-debt ratio of 17 percent by 2029. For investors, the combination of contracted demand and a large construction program creates a growth opportunity while keeping financing, regulation and execution in focus.

sum: Southern Company Prices $1.75 Billion 2026 Series A Equity Units Offering

Southern Company has priced an offering of 35 million 2026 Series A Equity Units, according to a press release issued by the company. Each unit carries a stated amount of $50, bringing the aggregate stated amount to $1.75 billion, and combines a contract to purchase Southern Company common stock in the future with fractional beneficial ownership interests in two series of remarketable senior notes.

The note components consist of a 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interest in Series 2026C Remarketable Senior Notes due 2031 with a $1,000 principal amount and a matching 1/40 interest in Series 2026D Remarketable Senior Notes due 2034, also with a $1,000 principal amount. Remarketing of each note series may begin no earlier than June 13, 2029. The offering is expected to close on November 17, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

Total annual distributions on the units are set at 8.625 percent, made up of interest on both note series and payments under the stock purchase contracts. The reference price is $92.47 per share, while the threshold appreciation price is $115.58 per share, a premium of roughly 25.0 percent over the reference price. Holders must purchase a variable number of common shares no later than December 15, 2029, or the next business day if that date falls on a non-business day.

Southern Company has granted the underwriters an option to buy up to 5 million additional units, representing an extra $250 million in aggregate stated amount, during the 13-day period starting on and including the initial issuance date. The option is intended solely to cover over-allotments.

Estimated net proceeds are approximately $1.724 billion, or $1.970 billion if the over-allotment option is fully exercised, after underwriting discounts and commissions but before other offering expenses. The company plans to direct about $135.3 million of the net proceeds toward repurchasing roughly $125.8 million in aggregate principal amount of its Series 2024A 4.50% Convertible Senior Notes due June 15, 2027. Those repurchases would occur through individually negotiated transactions with a limited number of holders, effected through one of the underwriters or an affiliate.

Southern Company stock faces renewed pension litigation in Georgia
sum: Southern Company faces a renewed pension dispute after a Georgia federal judge refused on Monday, November 9, 2026, to dismiss a proposed class action brought by company pensioners. The ruling allows claims over allegedly reduced annuity benefits to move toward discovery, according to Cohen Milstein, which summarized the Law360 report.

The proposed class includes former Southern Co. workers who allege that outdated actuarial assumptions were used when single-life annuities were converted into joint-and-survivor benefits. The retirees argue that older mortality tables produced lower payments than updated assumptions would have generated.

U.S. District Judge Steve C. Jones found that the allegations plausibly described a breach of fiduciary duties under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act. The claims also concern Southern Co.'s retirement plan committee, which the plaintiffs say knew that newer assumptions reflected longer life expectancy.

The order does not establish liability or determine damages. The judge also deferred the question of whether ERISA required the fiduciary to depart from pension-plan terms that allegedly conflicted with federal benefits law.

The case now moves toward discovery, leaving the potential financial and administrative consequences unresolved. For investors, the immediate issue is the continuation of the pension dispute rather than a concluded liability.

sum: Southern Company reported stronger third-quarter results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with adjusted earnings benefiting from warmer weather, higher customer usage and growing demand from large commercial and industrial customers. The company disclosed the figures in a PR Newswire release.

Southern Company reported third-quarter net income of 2.046 billion US dollars, up from 1.711 billion US dollars in the same period of 2025. Reported earnings per share rose to 1.77 US dollars from 1.55 US dollars. Excluding selected items, earnings increased to 2.242 billion US dollars, or 1.94 US dollars per share, from 1.766 billion US dollars, or 1.60 US dollars per share.

Operating revenue rose to 8.843 billion US dollars from 7.823 billion US dollars, an increase of 13.0 percent. The company attributed the improvement in adjusted earnings to warmer weather, increased usage, customer growth, higher revenue from large commercial and industrial customers and stronger earnings at Southern Power.

Those gains were partly offset by higher non-fuel operating expenses, higher taxes other than income taxes and dilution from additional shares outstanding. Southern Company also recorded charges tied to wind-facility repowering, debt extinguishment and estimated losses related to Nicor Gas capital investments.

Traditional electric operating companies remained the main earnings contributor. Their net income available to common shareholders rose to 2.272 billion US dollars from 1.920 billion US dollars. Southern Company Approves Rate Cut for Georgia Power Customers
sum: The Southern Company's SO subsidiary, the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC), has approved a plan that will lower overall electricity rates for Georgia Power customers, delivering meaningful savings to households and businesses across the state. Under the approved framework, a typical residential customer using 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity per month will save approximately $50 annually, equivalent to about $4.04 per month.

The decision is expected to generate total annual savings of roughly $285 million for Georgia Power's customer base, providing financial relief as energy consumption typically rises during the summer months.

Georgia PSC's approval follows a stipulated agreement inked between Georgia Power and the Public Interest Advocacy Staff of the Georgia PSC. The agreement addressed two regulatory proceedings filed earlier this year: the Fuel Cost Recovery case and the Storm Cost Recovery case.

These proceedings focused on recovering costs associated with fuel used to operate power generation facilities and expenses incurred while restoring electricity service following severe weather events, including Hurricane Helene in 2024. The approved plan balances cost recovery needs with customer affordability, enabling lower overall rates while maintaining reliable service.
Georgia PSC welcomed the commission's decision, emphasizing its ongoing efforts to operate efficiently and deliver dependable energy at competitive prices.

According to company leadership, the approved rate reduction comes at a critical time, helping customers manage electricity expenses during periods of higher seasonal demand. The decision follows months of regulatory review, public hearings and collaboration between the utility, PSC staff and other stakeholders.

For more than 140 years, Georgia PSC has served customers across the state, focusing on reliability and affordability. The company notes that since 1990, its rates have averaged approximately 15% below the national average.

sum: The build-out of data centers, not including IT hardware spending, is expected to cost about $1.7 trillion through the end of the decade, according to a study by McKinsey & Company. Southern Company (SO -1.07%) is uniquely positioned to benefit from that spending, driven by its geographic footprint, recent infrastructure completions, and a supportive regulatory environment.

The energy company serves 9 million customers and businesses through its subsidiaries, delivering electricity to Georgia, Alabama, and Mississippi, and natural gas to Georgia, Illinois, Virginia, and Tennessee.

The stock has significantly underperformed both the S&P 500 and the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF in total return over the past year. Here are three reasons why I think the stock is significantly oversold and presents an opportunity for investors.
The Southeast, particularly Georgia, has become a top destination for hyperscalers, such as Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft, looking for lower land and energy costs.

Southern Company recently increased its 2026-2030 capital spending plan to $81 billion in anticipation of that demand. The company has already fully contracted 10 gigawatts (GW) for large-load customers, much of it from gas turbines that can be brought online quickly as data centers ramp up, and Southern is anticipating a staggering 75 GW pipeline of potential data center interest.

Commercial electricity sales, which data centers drive, are expected to grow by roughly 20% annually through the end of the decade, according to CFO David P. Poroch, powering Southern's revenue growth.

The company was criticized in 2023 for huge cost overruns and delays for its Vogtle nuclear power plants near Waynesboro, Georgia. However, that spending is about to pay off. Data center operators have aggressive carbon-neutral goals but require steady reliability that solar and wind alone cannot provide without massive storage.

items.t: Southern Company reports fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 earnings
sum: ATLANTA, Feb. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Southern Company today reported fourth-quarter earnings of $416 million, or $0.38 per share, in 2025 compared with earnings of $534 million, or $0.49 per share, in the fourth quarter of 2024. Southern Company also reported full-year 2025 earnings of $4.3 billion, or $3.94 per share, compared with $4.4 billion, or $4.02 per share, in 2024.

Excluding the items described under "Net Income – Excluding Items" in the table below, Southern Company earned $612 million, or $0.55 per share, during the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with $544 million, or $0.50 per share, during the fourth quarter of 2024. For the full-year 2025, excluding these items, Southern Company earned $4.7 billion, or $4.30 per share, compared with $4.4 billion, or $4.05 per share, for 2024.

Adjusted earnings drivers for the full year 2025, as compared with 2024, were higher utility revenues, partially offset by higher non-fuel operations and maintenance expenses, depreciation and amortization, and interest expense.

Fourth-quarter 2025 operating revenues were $7.0 billion, compared with $6.3 billion for the fourth quarter of 2024, an increase of 10.1%. Operating revenues for the full year 2025 were $29.6 billion, compared with $26.7 billion in 2024, an increase of 10.6%.

"2025 was another outstanding year for Southern Company, and it was also a transformative one. Southern Company is meeting the growing demand responsibly, while continuing to deliver value and benefits to all of our customers," said Chris Womack, chairman, president and CEO. "Taking a disciplined, all-of-the-above approach is how we will continue to operate our company to serve this projected generational growth in a way that supports rate stability and helps drive long-term savings for our customers. Our nearly 30,000 employees remain committed to putting customers first, working every day to help keep costs down and provide reliable energy to the communities we are privileged to serve."
Southern Company's fourth-quarter and full-year earnings slides with supplemental financial information, including earnings guidance, are available at investor.southerncompany.com.
